history.headline: Yermo Ediciones publishes 'Muerte blanca' by Kid Toussaint and Iñaki Holgado inspired by real soldiers
history.summary: Yermo Ediciones released 'Muerte blanca', a war comic by Kid Toussaint and Iñaki Holgado, inspired by sniper Simo Häyhä and soldier Hiro Onoda. The story follows Riku, shaped by family trauma and war, evolving into a legendary sniper known as the White Death.

history.headline: Marvel replaces Marvel Unlimited with new Marvel Comics App developed with Webtoon
history.summary: Marvel is shutting down the Marvel Unlimited app, replacing it with a new Marvel Comics App co-created with Webtoon. The new app launches November 16, with Marvel Unlimited ending December 7. Registered users can import prior purchases. The new subscription will offer new comics one month after release, improving on Unlimited's three-month delay.

history.headline: Neon Ichiban 3.0 update adds in-app purchasing and Mac desktop digital collection support
history.summary: Neon Ichiban has launched version 3.0 of its app, re-enabling in-app purchasing on Apple and Android, easing comic buying. The update also expands its Mac desktop beta to allow importing DRM-free comics from various sources into a central digital collection, addressing digital ownership fragmentation.

history.headline: DC Studios co-heads Gunn and Safran to report directly to Skydance CEOs
history.summary: In the Skydance/WarnerMount merger, DC Studios co-heads James Gunn and Peter Safran remain in charge and will report directly to Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. This maintains their previous reporting arrangement under Warner Bros. Discovery. DC's prominent positioning in the corporate branding suggests a strong strategic importance in the new group, underscoring continued investment and focus on DC properties.

history.headline: French comics criticism magazines Bananas and Papiers nickelés maintain strong editorial presence despite distribution challenges
history.summary: Bananas, an annual critical comics magazine led by Évariste Blanchet, plans an autumn release with a varied rich editorial lineup including notable interviews and heritage discussions. Papiers nickelés, a quarterly directed by Yves Frémion, continues to publish insightful articles, including retrospectives on historical artists. However, Bananas faces distribution setbacks following the liquidation of the key distributor Makassar and now relies on direct orders for survival.

history.headline: DC Comics announces new Black Label and Vertigo series at NYCC 2026
history.summary: At New York Comic Con 2026, DC revealed multiple Black Label one-shots and miniseries. Highlights include 'Green Lantern: The Dying of the Light' by Jason Aaron and Tirso Cons, a gritty Hal Jordan story, and 'Joker/Harley: Malicious Intent.' Vertigo will publish 'Hide Nor Hair' by Adam Smith and Bob Quinn and material like 'Dreambound' transitioning from Webtoon to print. Established titles like '100 Bullets: Enemigos' and 'The Crying Doll' will continue publication in 2027.

history.headline: French comics magazines Bananas and Papiers nickelés continue strong editorial output despite distribution loss
history.summary: The annual comics criticism magazine Bananas, edited by Évariste Blanchet, will publish its autumn edition with a diverse lineup including interviews and historical retrospectives. The quarterly Papiers nickelés continues its work on comics heritage with articles on artists and genres. Bananas suffers distribution challenges after the liquidation of its main distributor Makassar and now relies on direct sales from the publisher for survival.

history.headline: Image Comics announces dark fantasy series Omen-Bound for March 2027
history.summary: At New York Comic-Con, Image Comics unveiled Omen-Bound, a new dark fantasy comic by Jim Zub and Alberto J. Alburquerque. The narrative features warriors and priests escorting a supernatural prisoner beyond reality, blending classic sword-and-sorcery with modern dramatic storytelling. A limited black-and-white preview was distributed onsite.

history.headline: Neyef's 'Les Enfants perdus' offers a grim reimagining of Peter Pan without fairy-tale magic
history.summary: Neyef (Romain Maufront) presents 'Les Enfants perdus,' a graphic novel depicting children fending for themselves in a ruined urban world, echoing a Peter Pan myth stripped of fantasy elements. The story explores themes of childhood lost, friendship, and fractured families as abandoned children struggle to survive and mimic adult roles in a harsh environment.

history.headline: LA Comic Con partners with StubHub for digital ticketing including free Neon Ichiban comic
history.summary: LA Comic Con has partnered with StubHub to offer digital ticket sales and resale, allowing attendees to purchase tickets with resale options. Tickets bought via StubHub include a free copy of Neon Ichiban's digital comic Absolute Batman #1 by Scott Snyder. Prices on StubHub are generally higher but add resale flexibility, while the convention retains control of ticketing. The free comic is delivered via a digital download code included with StubHub ticket purchases.

history.headline: Broken Frontier begins coverage for Thought Bubble Festival 2026
history.summary: Broken Frontier announces the start of its Thought Bubble Month 2026 coverage, promising daily articles on exhibitors, guests, and events leading up to the Harrogate-based festival. They encourage submissions for review by October 30 and note many featured comics may only be available at the convention itself, highlighting Thought Bubble's significance as an indie comics marketplace.

history.headline: Electronic Arts closes BioWare studio, cancels Mass Effect 5 after 30 years
history.summary: Electronic Arts (EA) announced it is laying off around 400 employees, including shutting down BioWare, the studio behind franchises like Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. This ends over 30 years of BioWare game development. The Mass Effect 5 project, which was in early development, has been officially cancelled as EA pivots to focus on other game genres.

history.headline: IDW partners with Blumhouse to publish comics based on popular Blumhouse films
history.summary: IDW Publishing announced an expansion of its IDW Dark line with licensed comics linked to Blumhouse Productions' horror films including 'The Purge' (written by Dan Watters, art by Juan José Ryp), 'M3GAN,' and 'Feliz día de tu muerte' scripted by Tim Seeley from a Scott Lobdell screenplay. This followed Blumhouse acquiring rights to adapt IDW's 'The Exorcism at 1600 Penn'.

history.headline: Rebellion to stage two-day immersive event celebrating 50 years of 2000 AD in March 2027
history.summary: Rebellion announced a special two-day immersive live event on 6-7 March 2027 at Protein Studios in Shoreditch, London, to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the British sci-fi comic 2000 AD. The event will include original programming, exclusive merchandise, legacy celebrations, and appearances by numerous creators who contributed over the comic's five-decade history.

history.headline: IDW announces expanded partnership with Blumhouse to publish comics based on Blumhouse films
history.summary: IDW Publishing will expand its IDW Dark line with comics adaptations of Blumhouse Productions' horror films including The Purge, M3GAN, and Feliz día de tu muerte. Notable creators involved include Dan Watters and Juan José Ryp on The Purge, and Tim Seeley adapting a Scott Lobdell original screenplay for Feliz día de tu muerte. This follows Blumhouse acquiring rights to adapt IDW's The Exorcism at 1600 Penn.

history.headline: IDW expands partnership with Blumhouse to produce comics based on popular horror films
history.summary: IDW Publishing announced an expanded deal with Blumhouse Productions to develop comics tied to Blumhouse's horror franchises, including The Purge (with Dan Watters and Juan José Ryp), M3GAN, and Feliz día de tu muerte (written by Tim Seeley from a Scott Lobdell script). This follows an earlier IDW comic IP, The Exorcism at 1600 Penn, being adapted by Blumhouse.

history.headline: Ellie Durkin's comic Seed expands its world and lore with full story release
history.summary: Ellie Durkin's Seed, set in the whimsical Squashed Forest, has released its longest comic story after several years of development. The expanded narrative deepens the magic system and lore, enriching the world with new characters like Trowl, Jessel, and Mandelbert. Durkin's artwork and panel design enhance the immersive reading experience, while playful humour and distinct visuals continue to define the title's charm.

history.headline: Leeds Comics Collective releases 'Warriors of Junk Food' anthology with 17 themed comic strips
history.summary: The Leeds Comics Collective has published its annual Thought Bubble anthology titled Warriors of Junk Food, featuring seventeen comic strips exploring a fast food theme. The collection showcases a mix of playful, satirical, and socially conscious stories from emerging and established creators, supporting community and collaboration within the small press scene.

history.headline: Joann Sfar launches promising youth comics collection 'Les Enchanteurs' at Les Arènes BD
history.summary: Joann Sfar leads a new collection called Les Enchanteurs at Les Arènes BD, focusing on contemporary reinterpretations of timeless stories, especially fairy tales. The collection debuts with albums like 'Niglo et le renard', a melancholy retelling of Little Thumb, and 'Le Seigneur des cailloux', a fantasy homage to Tolkien's Lord of the Rings. The stories explore themes of identity, family, and belonging with distinct artistic styles.

history.headline: Gladstone Investment Corp acquires majority stake in McFarlane Toys
history.summary: Gladstone Investment Corp has purchased a majority stake in McFarlane Toys, with co-owners Todd McFarlane and Stephen Tetrault remaining as shareholders and executives. Gladstone, a publicly traded business development company focusing on established middle market firms, plans to support McFarlane Toys' product innovation, new collectible categories, strategic licensing partnerships, and international growth. McFarlane Toys holds major licenses including Marvel, DC, Diablo, and Fallout.

history.headline: Cosmic Lighthouse launches as new UK graphic novel publisher at Thought Bubble 2026
history.summary: Cosmic Lighthouse, co-founded by Paul Cornell and Lee Harris, debuted as a UK publisher specializing in original graphic novels by renowned genre writers paired with top artists. Their first project adapts Martha Wells's The Murderbot Diaries and they hosted a launch event on November 13, 2026, at Thought Bubble Festival in Harrogate, including exclusive editions and creator signings.
